Mapping Global Student Agency: A Hierarchical Cluster Analysis of Goal-Setting, Help-Seeking, and STEM Performance in PISA 2025 (Markdown)

Tianyu Xu

2026-11-09

load student survey

library(haven)
library(dplyr)
## 
## Attaching package: 'dplyr'
## The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
## 
##     filter, lag
## The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
## 
##     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
student <- read_sav(
  "/Users/xutianyu/Downloads/PISA2025/CY09_MS_STU_PUF.sav", 
  encoding = "latin1"
)

extract the variables for this study

agency <- student %>%
  select(
    CNT,
    OECD,
    PV1MATH, PV1SCIE,
    ST432Q02DA, ST432Q03DA, ST432Q04DA, ST432Q06DA,
    ST433Q01DA, ST433Q02DA, ST433Q04DA, ST433Q06DA
  )

rename the variables

agency <- agency %>%
  rename(
    country = CNT,
    math_score = PV1MATH,
    science_score = PV1SCIE,
    
    plan_study    = ST432Q02DA,
    identify_gaps = ST432Q03DA,
    self_question = ST432Q04DA,
    adapt_strategy = ST432Q06DA,
    
    ask_classmates   = ST433Q01DA,
    ask_teachers     = ST433Q02DA,
    ask_general      = ST433Q04DA,
    ask_after_trying = ST433Q06DA
  )
ncol(agency)
## [1] 12

find NA proportion

library(tibble)

agency_na_prop <- agency %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), ~ mean(is.na(.x))))

#View(agency_na_prop)

use NA proportion = 0.5 as a threshold, make a table for all the countries

high_na_vars_per_country <- agency_na_prop %>%
  mutate(across(-country, ~ .x > 0.5)) %>%     
  mutate(Variables_Over_50pct_NA = rowSums(select(., -country))) %>% 
  select(country, Variables_Over_50pct_NA)           

#View(high_na_vars_per_country)
print(as_tibble(high_na_vars_per_country), n = Inf)

  filter(!country %in% countries_to_exclude)

  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), ~ mean(is.na(.x))))

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

country_means <- agency1 %>%
  group_by(country) %>% 
  summarise(
    plan_study       = mean(plan_study, na.rm = TRUE),
    identify_gaps    = mean(identify_gaps, na.rm = TRUE),
    self_question    = mean(self_question, na.rm = TRUE),
    adapt_strategy   = mean(adapt_strategy, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_classmates   = mean(ask_classmates, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_teachers     = mean(ask_teachers, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_general      = mean(ask_general, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_after_trying = mean(ask_after_trying, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# 2. OECD average
oecd_country_means <- agency1 %>%
  filter(OECD == 1) %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    plan_study       = mean(plan_study, na.rm = TRUE),
    identify_gaps    = mean(identify_gaps, na.rm = TRUE),
    self_question    = mean(self_question, na.rm = TRUE),
    adapt_strategy   = mean(adapt_strategy, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_classmates   = mean(ask_classmates, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_teachers     = mean(ask_teachers, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_general      = mean(ask_general, na.rm = TRUE),
    ask_after_trying = mean(ask_after_trying, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

oecd_means <- oecd_country_means %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "OECD_Mean")

# long format
long_means <- country_means %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -country, 
    names_to = "Variable", 
    values_to = "Mean_Value"
  )

# mark the countries with highest and lowest value for each variable
extremes <- long_means %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  filter(Mean_Value == max(Mean_Value, na.rm = TRUE) | 
         Mean_Value == min(Mean_Value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(Type = if_else(Mean_Value == max(Mean_Value, na.rm = TRUE), "Highest", "Lowest"))


var_levels <- c("plan_study", "identify_gaps", "self_question", "adapt_strategy",
                "ask_classmates", "ask_teachers", "ask_general", "ask_after_trying")
long_means$Variable <- factor(long_means$Variable, levels = var_levels)
extremes$Variable <- factor(extremes$Variable, levels = var_levels)
oecd_means$Variable <- factor(oecd_means$Variable, levels = var_levels)

# make the y-axis start from 1
baseline_val <- 1


p <- ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = long_means, 
               aes(x = Variable, xend = Variable, y = baseline_val, yend = Mean_Value, group = country), 
               color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.4) +

  geom_segment(data = extremes, 
               aes(x = Variable, xend = Variable, y = baseline_val, yend = Mean_Value, group = country), 
               color = "#2b83ba", linewidth = 0.8) +

  geom_point(data = data.frame(Variable = factor(var_levels, levels = var_levels)), 
             aes(x = Variable, y = baseline_val), 
             color = "#1f78b4", shape = 16, size = 3.5) +
  
  geom_point(data = oecd_means, 
             aes(x = Variable, y = OECD_Mean), 
             color = "#1f78b4", shape = 18, size = 5) +
  
  geom_text(data = oecd_means, 
            aes(x = Variable, y = OECD_Mean, label = "OECD average"), 
            hjust = -0.2, vjust = 0.5, size = 3, fontface = "bold", color = "#1f78b4") +
  
  geom_point(data = extremes, 
             aes(x = Variable, y = Mean_Value, color = Type), 
             shape = 15, size = 3) +
  
  geom_text(data = extremes, 
            aes(x = Variable, y = Mean_Value, label = country, color = Type), 
            hjust = -0.15, vjust = 0.5, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Highest" = "#d7191c", "Lowest" = "#2b83ba")) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, NA), breaks = seq(1, 4, by = 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.22))) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Goal Setting & Help Seeking: Perceived Agency",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean index",
    color = "Country Extremes"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1, face = "bold", size = 9),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

# create the goal setting variable
agency1 <- agency1 %>%
  mutate(goal_setting = plan_study + identify_gaps + self_question + adapt_strategy)

# figure out the bottom quarter and top quarter
country_quarter_means <- agency1 %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  mutate(
    goal_quartile = ntile(goal_setting, 4)
  ) %>%
  filter(goal_quartile %in% c(1, 4)) %>%
  group_by(country, goal_quartile) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_val = mean(goal_setting, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = goal_quartile,
    values_from = mean_val,
    names_prefix = "q_"
  ) %>%
  rename(Bottom_Quarter = q_1, Top_Quarter = q_4) %>%
  mutate(country = recode(country, !!!country_name_map))

# OECD average
oecd_subset <- agency1 %>%
  filter(OECD == 1) %>%
  mutate(goal_quartile = ntile(goal_setting, 4)) %>%
  filter(goal_quartile %in% c(1, 4)) %>%
  group_by(goal_quartile) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_val = mean(goal_setting, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

oecd_row <- data.frame(
  country        = "OECD average",
  Bottom_Quarter = oecd_subset$mean_val[oecd_subset$goal_quartile == 1],
  Top_Quarter    = oecd_subset$mean_val[oecd_subset$goal_quartile == 4]
)

plot_wide <- bind_rows(country_quarter_means, oecd_row)

# order countries by Top quarter ranking
plot_wide <- plot_wide %>%
  mutate(country = factor(country, levels = country[order(Top_Quarter, decreasing = FALSE)]))

non_oecd_levels <- setdiff(levels(plot_wide$country), "OECD average")
bottom_5_countries <- head(non_oecd_levels, 5)
top_5_countries    <- tail(non_oecd_levels, 5)

plot_wide <- plot_wide %>%
  mutate(
    row_group = case_when(
      country == "OECD average" ~ "OECD",
      country %in% top_5_countries ~ "Top 5",
      country %in% bottom_5_countries ~ "Bottom 5",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )

plot_long <- plot_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Bottom_Quarter, Top_Quarter),
    names_to = "Quartile",
    values_to = "Score"
  )

# add the shaded rows for OECD average (light blue), top 5, and bottom 5 (light green)
p <- ggplot(plot_wide, aes(y = country)) +
  
  geom_rect(data = filter(plot_wide, row_group == "Bottom 5"),
            aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = as.numeric(country) - 0.5, ymax = as.numeric(country) + 0.5),
            fill = "#e5f5e0", alpha = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +

  geom_rect(data = filter(plot_wide, row_group == "Top 5"),
            aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = as.numeric(country) - 0.5, ymax = as.numeric(country) + 0.5),
            fill = "#e5f5e0", alpha = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +

  geom_rect(data = filter(plot_wide, country == "OECD average"),
            aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = as.numeric(country) - 0.5, ymax = as.numeric(country) + 0.5),
            fill = "#c6dbef", alpha = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  
  geom_segment(aes(x = Bottom_Quarter, xend = Top_Quarter, y = country, yend = country), 
               color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  geom_point(data = plot_long, aes(x = Score, color = Quartile, shape = Quartile), size = 3) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Bottom_Quarter" = "#e6550d", "Top_Quarter" = "#3182bd"),
    labels = c("Bottom quarter of students' goal setting", "Top quarter of students' goal setting")
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("Bottom_Quarter" = 16, "Top_Quarter" = 18),
    labels = c("Bottom quarter of students' goal setting", "Top quarter of students' goal setting")
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Country-Level Student Goal-Setting Index by Quartile",
    x = "Goal-Setting Index Score",
    y = NULL,
    color = NULL,
    shape = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 8.5, 
      face = "bold",
      color = ifelse(levels(plot_wide$country) == "OECD average", "#08519c", "black")
    ),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
print(p)

Plot 3: Help seeking: dot plots for 4 variables

country_means <- agency1 %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    `Ask Classmates`     = mean(ask_classmates, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Ask Teachers`       = mean(ask_teachers, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Ask General`        = mean(ask_general, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Ask After Trying`   = mean(ask_after_trying, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(country = recode(country, !!!country_name_map))

# OECD average
oecd_means <- agency1 %>%
  filter(OECD == 1) %>%
  summarise(
    `Ask Classmates`     = mean(ask_classmates, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Ask Teachers`       = mean(ask_teachers, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Ask General`        = mean(ask_general, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Ask After Trying`   = mean(ask_after_trying, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(country = "OECD average")


plot_data <- bind_rows(country_means, oecd_means)


plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  mutate(
    overall_mean = (`Ask Classmates` + `Ask Teachers` + `Ask General` + `Ask After Trying`) / 4,
    country = factor(country, levels = country[order(overall_mean, decreasing = FALSE)])
  )


plot_long <- plot_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(`Ask Classmates`, `Ask Teachers`, `Ask General`, `Ask After Trying`),
    names_to = "Help_Seeking_Type",
    values_to = "Mean_Score"
  )


variable_highlights <- plot_long %>%
  filter(country != "OECD average") %>%
  group_by(Help_Seeking_Type) %>%
  arrange(Mean_Score) %>%
  mutate(
    rank_val = row_number(),
    max_rank = max(rank_val),
    highlight = case_when(
      rank_val <= 3 ~ "Bottom 3",
      rank_val >= max_rank - 2 ~ "Top 3",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


oecd_data <- plot_long %>%
  filter(country == "OECD average")

# 4. for each plot, mark top/bottom 3 shading countries (light green) and OECD shading (light blue)
p <- ggplot(plot_long, aes(x = Mean_Score, y = country, color = Help_Seeking_Type)) +

  geom_rect(data = filter(variable_highlights, highlight == "Bottom 3"),
            aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = as.numeric(country) - 0.5, ymax = as.numeric(country) + 0.5),
            fill = "#e5f5e0", alpha = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  

  geom_rect(data = filter(variable_highlights, highlight == "Top 3"),
            aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = as.numeric(country) - 0.5, ymax = as.numeric(country) + 0.5),
            fill = "#e5f5e0", alpha = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  

  geom_rect(data = oecd_data,
            aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = as.numeric(country) - 0.5, ymax = as.numeric(country) + 0.5),
            fill = "#c6dbef", alpha = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ Help_Seeking_Type, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(
    title = "Country_Level Student Help-Seeking Profiles",

    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(

Plot 4: scatterplot of math and science score

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

country_scores <- agency1 %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    math_score    = mean(math_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    science_score = mean(science_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(math_score) & !is.na(science_score)) %>%
  mutate(country = recode(country, !!!country_name_map))

# OECD average
oecd_scores <- agency1 %>%
  filter(OECD == 1) %>%
  summarise(
    math_score    = mean(math_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    science_score = mean(science_score, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

oecd_math <- oecd_scores$math_score
oecd_science <- oecd_scores$science_score

# mark countries in the first quadrant, whose math and science score are higher than OECD mean
country_scores <- country_scores %>%
  mutate(
    quadrant = case_when(
      math_score >= oecd_math & science_score >= oecd_science ~ "Above OECD (Both)", 
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )

p <- ggplot(country_scores, aes(x = math_score, y = science_score, label = country)) +

  geom_vline(xintercept = oecd_math, color = "#3182bd", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = oecd_science, color = "#3182bd", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +

  annotate("text", x = oecd_math, y = max(country_scores$science_score, na.rm = TRUE), 
           label = paste0("OECD average (", round(oecd_math, 1), ")"), color = "#08519c", fontface = "bold", size = 2, 
           angle = 90, vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0.9) +
  
  annotate("text", x = max(country_scores$math_score, na.rm = TRUE), y = oecd_science, 
           label = paste0("OECD average (", round(oecd_science, 1), ")"), color = "#08519c", fontface = "bold", size = 2, 
           vjust = -0.8, hjust = 0.7) +
  
  geom_point(aes(color = quadrant), size = 2.5, shape = 18) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Above OECD (Both)" = "#e6550d", "Other" = "#1f78b4")) +
  
  geom_text_repel(size = 3, box.padding = 0.3, point.padding = 0.3, max.overlaps = Inf) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Country-Level Mean Performance in Math and Science",
    x = "Mean Math Score",
    y = "Mean Science Score"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

print(p)

ggsave(filename = "/Users/xutianyu/Downloads/country_math_science_scatter.png", plot = p, width = 12, height = 20, dpi = 300)

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("hopach", update = FALSE, ask = FALSE)
## Bioconductor version 3.22 (BiocManager 1.30.27), R 4.5.3 (2026-03-11)
## Warning: package(s) not installed when version(s) same as or greater than current; use
##   `force = TRUE` to re-install: 'hopach'
selected_vars <- c("plan_study", "identify_gaps", "self_question", "adapt_strategy",                     
                   "ask_classmates", "ask_teachers", "ask_general", "ask_after_trying")

country_data <- agency1 %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    across(all_of(selected_vars), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),         
    math_score = mean(math_score, na.rm = TRUE),      
    science_score = mean(science_score, na.rm = TRUE)      
  )

# change into full country names
country_names_map <- country_name_map

country_data$Country_Name <- unname(country_names_map[country_data$country])
country_data$Country_Name[is.na(country_data$Country_Name)] <- country_data$country[is.na(country_data$Country_Name)]

# scale the dataset
data_matrix <- as.matrix(country_data %>% select(all_of(selected_vars)))
rownames(data_matrix) <- country_data$Country_Name
data.scale.subset <- scale(data_matrix)

# distance measures: uncentered correlation
uncenter.dist <- function(m) {
  as.dist(as.matrix(hopach::distancematrix(m, d = "cosangle")))
}

# agglomeration: average linkage
row.clus <- hclust(uncenter.dist(data.scale.subset), method = "ave")
col.clus <- hclust(uncenter.dist(t(data.scale.subset)), method = "ave")

# add annotation of math and science score on the right side
right_anno <- rowAnnotation(
  Math = country_data$math_score,
  Science = country_data$science_score,
  col = list(
    Math = colorRamp2(c(min(country_data$math_score, na.rm = TRUE), 
                       mean(country_data$math_score, na.rm = TRUE), 
                       max(country_data$math_score, na.rm = TRUE)), 
                     c("#edf8e5", "#a1d99b", "#238b45")),
    Science = colorRamp2(c(min(country_data$science_score, na.rm = TRUE), 
                           mean(country_data$science_score, na.rm = TRUE), 
                           max(country_data$science_score, na.rm = TRUE)), 
                         c("#f7fbff", "#a6bddb", "#2b8cbe"))
  ),
  simple_anno_size = unit(0.35, "cm"),
  annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8)
)

png("~/Downloads/agency_heatmap.png", width = 12, height = 12, units = "in", res = 300)
Heatmap(
  data.scale.subset, 
  name = "agency heatmap", 
  cluster_rows = row.clus,        
  cluster_columns = col.clus,     
  row_split = 4,
  column_split = 2,
  top_annotation = HeatmapAnnotation(
    foo = anno_block(
      gp = gpar(fill = c("#E41A1C", "#377EB8")),
      labels = c("Goal Setting", "Help Seeking"), 
      labels_gp = gpar(col = "white", fontsize = 10)
    )
  ),
  left_annotation = rowAnnotation(
    foo = anno_block(
      gp = gpar(fill = 2:5),
      labels = c("Low Goal / High Help", "Low Goal / Low Help", "Moderate Goal / Moderate Help", "High Goal / Low Help"), 
      labels_gp = gpar(col = "white", fontsize = 8)
    )
  ),
  right_annotation = right_anno,
  show_row_names = TRUE,          
  row_names_side = "right",       
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 7),      
  column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 9),  
  column_title = "Hierarchical Clustering Analysis of perceived agency PISA 2025",
  column_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold")
)
